title: Selector Phase of the Tabulation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and write $n$ for the number of selector states in its tabulation. For every Boolean string $y$, every $m<n$, and every $m\le |y|$, after $m$ steps the tabulated machine is in selector state $m$, with the first $m$ selector bits equal to the corresponding bits of $y$ and all remaining bits false. Its input head is at position $\min(m+1,|y|+1)$ in the input tape convention with boundary blanks; all work tapes and the three auxiliary tapes are blank, their heads are at the origin, and the output is empty.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine with Boolean alphabet
$m<n$, where $n$ is the number of selector states
